newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks firm, prices seen rising further.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks firm, prices seen rising further.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed firmer on Tuesday in active trade spearheaded by Zagrebacka Banka, which hit a record 2,410 kuna during the session.

"The trade is unusually active, especially if we compare it to the same period of last year. I think that the rise in share prices will continue," an analyst at I.C.F. consultancy and brokerage told Reuters.
Only three of 18 active issues fell, while 11 rose and four were flat. Volume shrank slightly to 19,817 units, but turnover rose to 14.8 million kuna from Friday's 12.3 million.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka's ordinaries spiced up the day's activity, closing at 2,400 kuna on volume of 2,217 units.
Another blue chip Pliva stirred quite a bit of interest, selling 3,678 shares to close one kuna higher at 561.
"Buyers are showing interest for both blue chips and this will remain so. The reason may be that some of the half-year results have leaked," the analyst explained.
But he said both Pliva's and Zagrebacka's future prices hinged on the developments on the London Stock Exchange.
Zagrebacka's 1/10 global depositary receipts (GDRs) rose to $37.25 from $36.25 on Seaq International.
Pliva's GDRs, representing 1/5 of each share, fetched $17.525 compared to $17.425 at close on Monday.
The day's biggest gainer was Chile's Cervecerias subsidiary -- Karlovacka Pivovara brewery -- adding 50 kuna or 9.1 percent to end at 600 kuna on volume of 2,551 shares.
It was expected to continue rising in the coming days.
Food-processor Podravka, selling 4,841 shares, was the most active issue. It rose two kuna to 262.
"Podravka has picked up and is rising from the pits. Still, it may be traded even more," the analyst said.
The biggest loser, ship repairer Viktor Lenac, lost seven kuna or 3.8 percent to 173 kuna with 492 shares sold.
"It looks like the Lenac price is stabilising but I think its stock will see a lot of trading," said the analyst.
